items.answer: In practical virtual reality (VR) development, a developer may use a software development kit (SDK) for a particular headset or platform to handle lowest-level, platform-specific operations such as device drivers, head tracking, and display output; SDKs are platform dependent, with a platform being a combination of hardware and operating system (OS), and the developer may not handle the lowest-level operations directly but must understand the SDK that handles them.
An authoring tool for a game engine lets a developer access the different functionalities supported by the game engine in order to develop their own software that runs on top of the game engine.
Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Marker-based augmented reality (AR) applications use markers placed in the environment to trigger an augmented experience, and when a device detects a marker, the desired digital content appears at that marker's position in the real-world view.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.
In 1997, computer-vision techniques were used to overlay augmented reality (AR) content on real-world markers, and tracking was used to register the AR content in three dimensions.
